dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1787 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 240 items printed somewhere), and the families of 1786 were looked for on the 1787 pages (none reach them). Every item in 3 or more papers was counted by its own opening over all 1,297 pages in both transcriptions and merged into text units (33 of 123 met the bar); every page was swept for seven-word sequences shared by 4 or more papers, read with the stricter coverage test of 24 November (97 passages no item covers); every unit and passage that meets the bar was read, and the chosen items' openings were searched over all pages.
dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (register Y-THIN) as amended by the owner's choice B1 on 23 November 2026: an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks, and by at least 4; digests are not. As in R-01, items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted, and the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (about 20 to 35, a target, not a quota); one affair's items as in X-1800-01. The eligible items not chosen are listed with their counts and are not checked against the scans. Sub-stories (C-01), private persons (R-04) and the list of items read and not admitted (R-03) apply as in every year.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1787 has 10 catalogue series, which are 7 papers (C-04): the New-York Packet; the Independent Journal (New York); the New-York Journal (the weekly register to 8 November, then the daily patriotic register); the Daily Advertiser (New York, from 1 October, under two catalogue numbers); the New-Hampshire Gazette (Portsmouth, Fowle's to 2 June, then under a second number); the Kentucke Gazette (Lexington, from 18 August); and the Pennsylvania Packet, and Daily Advertiser (Philadelphia, one issue, 19 September). The release's map lists no misfiled RevX page for 1787; three issues are filed under another date (X-1787-02).

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Every finder item of 1787 in 3 or more papers (and of 1786 over the 1787 pages: none) was counted by its own opening over all 1,297 pages in both transcriptions and merged into text units: 33 of 123 units met the bar, of which 7 are advertisements and legal notices and 13 are parts of the Constitution. Reading them, with the sweep's passages, gave 25 items read: 15 eligible and 10 below the bar (with The Federalist's numbers, each in 3 papers, as one line). Three are printed by every paper that survives for their weeks and are admitted; 10 are chosen (13 stories, 13 groups, 54 printings); 1 eligible item is listed as not chosen and 1 for the owner.
counted_item_by_item.The bar: Y-THIN: more than half of the papers that survive for the item's weeks (a surviving issue between its first and last printing, and at least in the three weeks from its first printing), and at least 4. 1787 has 7 papers: 4 are in print from January to April, 3 in May and June, 4 or 5 in July and August, and 6 from September to December (7 when the Pennsylvania Packet, and Daily Advertiser's one issue, 19 September, falls in an item's weeks); the bar is 4, and no item can reach it in May and June.
counted_item_by_item.Letters printed together: A letter and the papers it sends are one item (X-1810-01): the Constitution, the Convention's resolutions and General Washington's letter (the Independent Journal's supplement prints the letter first); Mr. Jay's letter and the note that sends it to the printer (the New-Hampshire Gazette prints the letter without the note).
counted_item_by_item.Printed with other time words: The April paragraph on Congress's resolution (the New-Hampshire Gazette dates it 'April 14' and reads 'Yesterday' for 'On Friday last') and the October paragraph on the judges of the western territory ('yesterday', 'Tuesday last', 'On the 16th instant') are counted as one item each: the words are the same apart from the time.
counted_item_by_item.Printed again: C-08: the New-Hampshire Gazette reports the judges of the western territory again on 9 November, in its own words under Portsmouth.
counted_item_by_item.Pages that quote an item or print a late: Not counted (C-07): the Daily Advertiser's printing of Congress's resolution of 21 February inside an essay by Cato (15 October); the New-York Journal's essays that quote the Constitution at length (18 October and later); the reports of the Pennsylvania convention that quote Mr. Mason's objections. Not counted (C-06): the Kentucke Gazette's printing of only the later articles of the treaty with Morocco (18 August, 'continued from our last'); the New-Hampshire Gazette's printing of only the later part of the requisition, with the quotas (21 November).
counted_item_by_item.The Kentucke Gazette filed twice: The Kentucke Gazette is filed twice for most of its issues (editions 1 and 2, two copies of the same issue); a paper is counted once, and the ledger uses edition 1 unless its page is filed under another date.

not_admitted.The ratification of the Constitution by: By its own words below the bar for its weeks (3 papers, needs 4).
not_admitted.Petersburg, 6 December 1787: 'the Indian: By its own words below the bar for its weeks (3 papers, needs 4). The New-Hampshire Gazette (28 November) prints a Baltimore paragraph with the same words.

not_admitted.Advertisements, legal notices and formul: Not news items (C-10): insolvent and absent debtors' notices, a decree in chancery, notices of sales, merchants' and makers' advertisements (among them the New-York Air Furnace and a druggists' list), the assize of bread, theatre bills, a society's meeting notices, and recurring formulas of headings and requests to printers. They were read and not counted; the notices name private persons, so they are listed by count only (R-04).

for_the_owner.A Pittsburgh report: a young Seneca man: Eligible: printed by 4 of the 7 papers that survive for its weeks (IJ, KG, NHG, NYP); it turns on a private person (R-04) and is not chosen; listed without names. Not checked against the scans.

for_user_decision.The papers in print, the bar and the cho: As built: Y-THIN as amended (B1), with 7 papers (10 catalogue series; three papers stand under two numbers each, C-04); the bar of 4 makes 15 items eligible. Three are printed by every paper in print and admitted; 10 others are chosen (13 stories, 13 groups, 54 printings); one is listed as not chosen and one for the owner.
for_user_decision.Choosing among the eligible items (X-178: As built: every eligible item is chosen except the Philadelphia paragraph on Mr. Gerry and Mr. Mason (October), of the affair of the Constitution in the same weeks (X-1800-01). No item is eligible from January to March or in May and June; the call for the Convention (Congress, 21 February) stands in 3 of the 4 papers in print.
for_user_decision.Pages filed under another date (X-1787-0: As built: the Independent Journal's supplement of 22 September (filed with the issue of 12 September), the New-York Packet of 5 October (filed with 2 October) and the Kentucke Gazette's pages of 13 October (filed also under 6 October) keep the release's page keys; their printings carry notes with the printed dates. A filing correction, as in v0.11.7 and v0.11.13, can date them as printed at the owner's word.
for_user_decision.Private persons (X-1787-03): As built (R-04): the Pittsburgh report of a young Seneca man's death among the smallpox (4 of 7) turns on one man and is listed for the owner without names; it can be admitted at the owner's word.
for_user_decision.Advertisements and legal notices (X-1787: As built (C-10): seven text units over the bar, and many sweep passages, are advertisements, legal notices and formulas; they are not news items and are not counted. The New York dailies print the same notices for weeks.
for_user_decision.The Federalist (X-1787-05): As built: each number of The Federalist printed in 1787 stands in 3 papers (the Independent Journal, the New-York Packet and the Daily Advertiser), below the bar of 4; they are listed as one line.
